title: Fmpz Private Helper Protocol
objective: Authenticate intentionally private same-source helpers in native artifacts so strict native loading permits their ordinary direct Python fallback while preserving direct internal compiled calls and rejecting genuinely missing or tampered functions

oracles: same-source dynamic fallback compared with compiled public entry execution
authenticated production cubic closure metadata and strict autoload

handoff.summary: Native IR v38 now records lexical @native provenance independently of subset-selection mode. The compiler derives a canonical private-function list only from lexical, non-host-callable functions whose provenance is the artifact's own physical source; imported and undecorated helpers are excluded. That list participates in standalone discovery compatibility, generated wrapper registration and inspection, production cache records, and production-pack identity and manifests. Runtime loading validates canonical names, rejects callable/private overlap, compares index and wrapper metadata before resolving a missing export, and returns a frozen identity sentinel only for authenticated membership. The @native decorator recognizes only that exact sentinel, so private helpers remain ordinary callable Python with is_native=True, is_compiled=False, and execution_mode='dynamic' under strict mode, while internal native calls remain direct and no aggregate ABI is published. The real cubic closure records 83 functions, 61 private functions, 14 lexical-private functions, excludes its one imported lexical-private function, and authenticates exactly 13 same-source helpers. Independent review found no correctness, identity, or fail-closed blocker. A clean production build rebuilt all 39 kernel families; focused standalone plus production tests pass 12/12 and strict baselib passes with zero errors.
risks: Native Windows x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64 remain required CI validation hosts; the protocol itself uses only generated JSON metadata, JavaScript sets, and existing wrapper/runtime boundaries.
The shared optimizer-opportunity manifest is intentionally not regenerated in this lane and makes the final architecture aggregate stop after its native and Wasm subchecks pass.

The integrated base has pre-existing exact-range regression drift in exact-arena temporary-name expectations and a reusable-workspace symbol-size probe; these are unrelated to private-helper resolution and remain for the dedicated regression lane.
The concurrently claimed test/number-field-cubic-native-class-number.cjs still expects IR v37 and must be mechanically updated to v38 by the cubic acceptance lane after rebasing.
next_steps: Rebase the cubic all-83 acceptance lane onto this commit, update its single IR-version assertion to v38, and prove the complete strict production execution and exact replay.
Regenerate shared optimizer and Wasm identity artifacts once the compiler series is integrated, then let all required platform CI validate the new artifact metadata.
